source.title: Giuseppe Pitrè, Feste patronali in Sicilia
source.series: Biblioteca delle tradizioni popolari siciliane, volume XXI
source.author_preface_self_report: Pitrè reports 60 feast descriptions spanning 92 municipalities, soliciting correspondents through printed questionnaires; source author is one historical compiler with mixed direct and indirect information.
source.source_reliability_limit: OCR may contain character/date/location errors; original edition image cannot currently be read through source viewer. Specific printed page numbers are not certified per observation.

methodology: Directly read Italian OCR segments in original 1900 print (unlike prior posthumous Palermo volumes); manually paraphrase source-bound actions with Archive displayed line locators. Each row is a descriptive source/detail observation, NOT verified distinct practice identity. A single feast may span 10–30 details. Pitrè repeats some 1881 observations, quotes eighteenth-century historians, correspondents and legends; no independent corroboration without reading their originals. Ritual approval, chronological continuity and scan-based OCR accuracy held. Some object and civic segments are retained as context, while supernatural folklore is explicitly not endorsed.
